text:
sam: heads-up — Support ticket #C-4021 reporting high p95/p99 for api.redwood.ai in eu-west starting ~10:20 UTC. Customer sees 400–800ms extra tail latency.
anika: saw the alert too. Grafana shows p95 jump at 10:19, p99 at 10:21. Throughput steady.
matt: can we confirm it's network and not a model cold-start? token times look normal. Any TLS errors in logs?
irina: searching auth/proxy logs now. Quick grep: `grep \"TLS handshake failed\" proxy.log | sed -n '1,50p'` — a handful of `read timeout` from 10:18–10:24, mostly from eu-west-2 nodes.
sam: curious — traceroutes from our health checks to customer IP show an extra hop through an intermediary AS around that window. Could be transient route pivot.
opsbot: [probe-run] eu-west health probe to api.redwood.ai -> avg rtt 28ms, p99 233ms at 10:22 UTC (probe-id: p-8732)
anika: DNS TTL check: customer resolves api.redwood.ai to 3 records; one has an unexpectedly low TTL (30s) while others 300s. Could cause inconsistent POP selection on resolver side.
matt: can you paste the dig output?
anika: ```
; <<>> DiG 9.10.6 <<>> api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.ai. 30 IN A 35.187.5.12
api.redwood.ai. 300 IN A 3.120.45.10
api.redwood.ai. 300 IN A 18.194.22.9
```
irina: that 30s one maps to eu-west-2 cached entry. If a resolver flips rapidly between those IPs while our edge routes are imbalanced, clients could see higher latency. Also seeing increased TLS resumption misses on the 35.187.5.12 path.
sam: hypothesis: outbound BGP flap at one egress caused some traffic to prefer the 35.187.5.12 pop which had higher cross-az hops, plus the short TTL allowed fast switches, producing the p99 spike.
matt: can we mitigate quickly? Suggestions: 1) add a short-term DNS record reprioritization to de-weight the problematic IP 2) enable sticky routing at the proxy for this customer 3) ask customer to flush resolver cache (if enterprise).
anika: rolling a quick DNS weight change now — reducing weight of 35.187.5.12 via our DNS control plane (propagation should be <60s). Watch probes.
opsbot: [dns-change] Weight update submitted for ip 35.187.5.12 -> weight 10 (was 100). Change-id d-4421
irina: also pushing a proxy config tweak to prefer TLS session caching for that customer’s route (canary to 5% first). Patch: `proxy.cfg: prefer_session_cache: true for route: /v1/customers/C-4021`
sam: good. Monitor p95/p99 and health probes.
opsbot: [metric-alert] p99 for C-4021 dropped from 820ms -> 160ms over next 90s (alert cleared).
matt: can confirm from traces: requests that stayed on 3.120.45.10 show stable latencies ~40ms. Those hitting 35.187.5.12 were high and had an extra ASN hop.
anika: follow-ups: 1) coordinate with network team to check egress peer for 35.187.5.12 2) extend TTL consistency across our A records (avoid one-outlier low TTL) 3) consider automatic DNS de-weighting based on probe anomalies.
irina: filing a post-incident ticket with traceroutes, TLS logs, and the DNS weight change diff. Also attaching repro steps for support: how to force resolver to that IP and run `traceroute -n` + `openssl s_client -connect ip:443 -sess_out sess.bin`.
sam: thanks team — customer support notified they can close the escalation if metrics remain stable. Leaving this thread open for network team follow-up. :thumbsup:
